production_surfaces.notes: Async TCP, DNS/address resolution, stream ownership, split halves, half-close, close, limits, typed errors.
Rustls-backed TLS configs and async streams with safe verification defaults, mTLS, SNI, ALPN, and typed errors.
Typed URL/query/percent primitives; non-UTF-8 and Unicode/IDNA behavior blocked on text/i18n provider milestones.
Method, status, version, headers, request/response heads, body streams, typed HTTP errors, and transport substrate.

deferred_or_rejected_surfaces.rationale: No named near-term production datagram consumer plus fixture-insufficiency rationale was recorded in M0.
deferred_or_rejected_surfaces.revisit_rule: A future issue must name the production consumer and prove TCP/TLS/HTTP fixtures are insufficient.

deferred_or_rejected_surfaces.rationale: Descriptor-shaped CPython socket API conflicts with typed async stream ownership.
deferred_or_rejected_surfaces.revisit_rule: Only Sifr-native additions to sifr.net may revisit socket capabilities.

deferred_or_rejected_surfaces.rationale: TLS is exposed through typed config and streams, not SSLContext/SSLSocket compatibility.
deferred_or_rejected_surfaces.revisit_rule: Only Sifr-native TLS requirements may revisit.

deferred_or_rejected_surfaces.rationale: Manual selector readiness and raw event-loop policies are internal.
deferred_or_rejected_surfaces.revisit_rule: Requires a separate low-level readiness architecture issue.

deferred_or_rejected_surfaces.rationale: URL parsing/building is typed; opener/request policy belongs to the future HTTP client phase.
deferred_or_rejected_surfaces.revisit_rule: Future client APIs must be Sifr-native.

deferred_or_rejected_surfaces.rationale: CPython-shaped client/server products are not substrate and handler subclasses are rejected.
deferred_or_rejected_surfaces.revisit_rule: Phase 41 and the future HTTP client phase own public product APIs.

deferred_or_rejected_surfaces.rationale: QUIC runtime/security strategy is outside this substrate.
deferred_or_rejected_surfaces.revisit_rule: Open a transport issue after HTTP/2 substrate closes.

m0_decisions.outcome: single-runtime-worker per process for this phase; multi-core throughput follow-up owns scale strategy

m0_decisions.evidence: No named production consumer and insufficiency rationale recorded.

m0_decisions.outcome: sifr.http owns substrate types; sifr.http.core is rejected
m0_decisions.evidence: Avoids duplicate stable namespace layers for Phase 41 and HTTP client handoff.

m0_decisions.outcome: ByteBuffer placeholder resolves to Sifr built-in bytes; no import required for the type, helper namespace is sifr.bytes
m0_decisions.evidence: Existing built-in bytes value model is owned and immutable; network/TLS/HTTP signatures use bytes.

m0_decisions.outcome: priority has no public API in v1; unknown extension frames are ignored only after frame accounting or map to ProtocolError with unsupported-extension-frame evidence
m0_decisions.evidence: HTTP/2 conformance inventory owns exact fixture selection.

m0_decisions.outcome: TlsStream.close and TlsWriteHalf.close consume their handle, attempt close_notify first, flush accepted plaintext/alert before success, and preserve cancellation or lower-transport evidence on failure
deferred from public API until serving-scale follow-up closes
